note: Example prompts on the web demo, all from the test split of data/prompts.jsonl, grouped by what the cascade does with them at the default threshold (0.28). Picked on 2026-11-17: Jev checked the small model's answers to all 200 test prompts, then each candidate ran through the full cascade twice with the models in config.deploy.yaml (openai/gpt-oss-20b small, openai/gpt-oss-120b large, on Groq). Only prompts that behaved the same way both times are listed; the Jev scores in the comments are the two runs. Model output can still vary between runs, and the groups must be re-checked if the models change.

groups.name: pass
groups.title: Jev passes a right answer
groups.hint: The small model is right, Jev agrees, and the large model is never called.

groups.name: catch
groups.title: Jev catches a wrong answer
groups.hint: The small model is wrong, Jev flags it, and the large model gets it right.

groups.name: catch_unfixed
groups.title: Jev catches it, but the large model is wrong too
groups.hint: Escalating is the right call, but it does not help: both models miss these.

groups.name: miss
groups.title: Jev misses a wrong answer
groups.hint: Jev rates the wrong answer as probably fine, so it reaches the user. Drag the threshold below Jev's score to escalate it.

examples.label: SNMP tools
examples.comment: p_wrong 0.17, 0.18; the large model is also wrong

groups.name: false_alarm
groups.title: Jev flags a right answer
groups.hint: A false alarm. On tomato vines the large model is also right; on hypotheses it answers wrongly, so escalating makes the result worse.
